title: Hall Effect Measurement Simulator
description: Top view of a silicon Hall bar carrying a current in a perpendicular magnetic field. Carriers are pushed toward one face, charge builds up, and a voltmeter shows the Hall voltage. A panel extracts the Hall coefficient, carrier type, carrier concentration, resistivity, and Hall mobility. Switching between n-type and p-type or flipping the field reverses the sign of the Hall voltage.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics

educational.topic: Hall effect measurement of carrier type, concentration, and mobility
learningObjectives: Explain why the sign of the Hall voltage depends on the carrier type
Calculate the carrier concentration from Hall measurement data
Distinguish n-type from p-type material from the sign of the Hall coefficient

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with a real-time device view, measurement readouts, and an optional carrier animation
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students predict the deflection direction and the sign of the Hall voltage, then check; partners extract the parameters of an unknown sample
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the face toward which carriers are pushed
Calculate carrier concentration from the Hall voltage
Identify the carrier type of an unknown sample from the sign of the Hall coefficient

controls.label: Start / Pause
controls.purpose: Run the carrier animation; the simulation loads paused

simulationModel.modelType: physics-based, steady state; qualitative carrier animation
equations: F = q (v x B); q E_H = q v_d B
V_H = I B / (q n t) in magnitude
R_H = V_H t / (I B) = -1/(q n) or +1/(q p)
rho = V_x W t / (I L); mu_H = |R_H| / rho
assumptions: Silicon bar 6 mm x 2 mm x 0.5 mm at 300 K
Single carrier type, full ionization, no compensation
V_H measured as the -y face minus the +y face
limitations: No two-carrier conduction, magnetoresistance, or contact misalignment voltage
Dot speed and surface-charge counts are on logarithmic, not linear, scales
